oaths-of-strasbourg.s: The Oaths of Strasbourg were mutual pledges of alliance sworn in 842 CE by Louis the German and Charles the Bald, grandsons of Charlemagne, against their brother Lothair. They were recorded in early Romance and Germanic vernaculars so that each army could understand them.

oba-dynasty.s: The Oba dynasty is the royal line of the Kingdom of Benin, traditionally dated from about 1180 CE when Eweka I was installed after the Ogiso line lost legitimacy. The early Obas centralised royal authority against the hereditary uzama nobles.

obelisk.s: An obelisk is a tall, narrow, tapering stone monument, often carved from a single block. In the Aksumite Empire, monumental stelae of this kind were erected at the capital Aksum, the largest standing over 33 metres tall according to the site's profile.

occupation-of-bosnia-herzegovina.s: The occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina was the entry of Austro-Hungarian troops into the Ottoman provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1878, authorised by the Congress of Berlin. The army had to overcome armed local resistance during the pacification.

occupation-of-istanbul.s: The occupation of Istanbul was the military occupation of the Ottoman capital by Allied forces following the empire's defeat in the First World War, beginning in 1918. It symbolised the collapse of Ottoman sovereignty.

occupation-of-japan.s: The occupation of Japan was the Allied occupation of the country after its surrender in 1945, directed by the United States. It introduced sweeping political, legal and economic reforms, including a new constitution.

october-manifesto.s: The October Manifesto was a declaration issued by Tsar Nicholas II in 1905 under pressure from revolution. It promised civil liberties and created the State Duma as an elected legislative assembly.

oda-nobunaga.s: Oda Nobunaga was a Japanese warlord of the sixteenth century who began the military unification of Japan during the Sengoku period. Tokugawa Ieyasu served as his ally.

oder-river.s: The Oder is a river of central Europe flowing north through present-day Czechia, Poland and Germany into the Baltic Sea. Sweden secured its mouth in Pomerania during the Thirty Years' War in the 1630s.

odessa.s: Odessa is a port city on the Black Sea coast of present-day Ukraine, founded under Catherine the Great in the 1790s. It grew rapidly as the main outlet for grain grown on the steppe of southern Russia and Ukraine.

odoacer.s: Odoacer was a Germanic military leader who deposed Romulus Augustulus, the last Western Roman emperor, on 4 September 476 CE. He sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople and ruled Italy as king.

oduduwa.s: Oduduwa is the legendary progenitor of the Yoruba peoples and the founding ruler of Ile-Ife in Yoruba tradition. Many Yoruba dynasties trace their descent from him.

ogaden.s: The Ogaden is a plateau and lowland region in the Horn of Africa, today forming part of eastern Ethiopia. Its pastoral hinterland supplied livestock for export and recruits for the Adal Sultanate's armies, drawn largely from Somali and Afar nomads.

ogboni-society.s: The Ogboni society was a religious and judicial institution among the Yoruba, devoted to the earth cult. In the Oyo Empire its membership cut across political hierarchies.

ogedeid-khanate.s: The Ögedeid khanate refers to the domains of the descendants of Ögedei Khan in Central Asia, which became a significant power under Kaidu in the late thirteenth century. In alliance with Duwa of the Chagatai Empire, Kaidu waged sustained wars against Kublai Khan's Yuan dynasty.

oghuz-turks.s: The Oghuz Turks were a confederation of Turkic tribes who lived on the steppes north of the Caspian and Aral seas. In the eleventh century the Seljuks, from the Qiniq clan of the Oghuz, built the Seljuk Empire and opened Anatolia to Turkic settlement.

ogiso-dynasty.s: The Ogiso dynasty, whose name means Kings of the Sky, was the earliest ruling line of the Edo kingdom centred on Ubini, later Benin City. It governed for several centuries before losing legitimacy in a period of crisis.

oguola.s: Oguola was an Oba of Benin in the late thirteenth century, dated by the site to c. 1274–1287.

oil-palm.s: The oil palm is a tree native to West and Central Africa whose fruit yields palm oil, an important food and trade product. It was cultivated across the forest and savanna zones of the region.

oirats.s: The Oirats are a group of western Mongol peoples who became a major power on the Mongolian and Central Asian steppe from the fifteenth century. They raided the eastern lands of Moghulistan, the successor state of the Chagatai Empire.

ojigi.s: Ojigi was an Alaafin, or king, of the Oyo Empire in the early eighteenth century. In the 1720s he subjugated Dahomey after King Agaja disrupted the coastal slave trade network managed by Oyo's tributaries.

okomfo-anokye.s: Okomfo Anokye was an Akan priest who, with Osei Tutu, founded the Ashanti Empire around 1700. Tradition holds that he conjured the Golden Stool from the heavens, which became the sacred symbol of Asante unity.

old-assyrian-period.s: The Old Assyrian period is the earliest phase of Assyrian history, from about 2025 BCE, when Assur emerged as an independent city-state. It was characterised by a commercial network of merchant colonies in Anatolia, centred on Kanesh, trading tin and textiles for silver.

old-babylonian-empire.s: The Old Babylonian Empire, or First Dynasty of Babylon, was an Amorite state in central Mesopotamia that grew to dominate the region under Hammurabi in the eighteenth century BCE. It is known for the Code of Hammurabi and the elevation of Marduk as supreme god.

old-french.s: Old French is the form of the French language spoken from around the ninth to the fourteenth century. It developed from the spoken Latin of the western Frankish lands.

old-high-german.s: Old High German is the earliest recorded stage of the German language, used from about the eighth to the eleventh century. It was spoken in the eastern Frankish realm of the Carolingian Empire.

old-hittite-kingdom.s: The Old Hittite Kingdom was the first phase of Hittite statehood in central Anatolia, established around 1650 BCE with Hattusa as its capital. Its early kings expanded into northern Syria, and Mursili I raided Babylon around 1595 BCE.

old-khmer.s: Old Khmer is the earliest recorded form of the Khmer language, used in inscriptions in Cambodia from the seventh century. In the Khmer Empire it was used alongside Sanskrit in stone inscriptions.

old-malay.s: Old Malay is the earliest attested form of the Malay language, known from inscriptions in Sumatra and nearby regions. The Kedukan Bukit inscription of 682 CE, found near Palembang, is the oldest surviving example.

old-persian.s: Old Persian is the ancient Iranian language of the Achaemenid kings, written in a cuneiform script. It appears in royal inscriptions such as the Behistun Inscription of Darius I.

olive-oil.s: Olive oil is the oil pressed from olives, a staple of Mediterranean diet, lighting and trade since antiquity. In the Macedonian Empire it was among the products of Macedon's agrarian economy.

oljeitu.s: Öljeitü was a ruler of the Ilkhanate in the early fourteenth century. He built the great domed mausoleum at Sultaniyya around 1313, a landmark of Persian-Islamic architecture.

oman.s: Oman is a country on the south-eastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula, commanding the approaches to the Persian Gulf. In antiquity it was known as Magan, a source of copper traded with Mesopotamia in the age of the Akkadian Empire.

omar-khayyam.s: Omar Khayyam was a Persian mathematician, astronomer and poet of the eleventh and early twelfth centuries. He worked under the patronage of the Seljuk sultan Malik Shah and took part in reforming the solar calendar with great astronomical precision.

omo-noba.s: Omo n'Oba is a title of the Oba of Benin, rendered on the site as child of the king of kings. It expressed the Oba's sacred authority as king, high priest and embodiment of the state's continuity.

opium-wars.s: The Opium Wars were two conflicts between Qing China and Western powers, chiefly Britain, in 1839–1842 and 1856–1860. Arising from British efforts to force open Chinese markets, including to the opium trade, they ended in Qing defeat.

opoku-ware-i.s: Opoku Ware I was the Asantehene, or ruler of the Ashanti Empire, from about 1720 to 1750, succeeding Osei Tutu. His campaigns greatly expanded the empire's territory.

orang-laut.s: The Orang Laut, or sea people, are communities of maritime nomads who have long lived on boats in the waters around Sumatra, the Riau islands and the Malay Peninsula. They formed the core naval force of the Srivijaya Empire.

oranmiyan.s: Oranmiyan is a legendary Yoruba prince, described in oral tradition as the youngest son of Oduduwa. Tradition credits him with founding the Oyo Empire in the savannah north of the forest zone.

orban.s: Orban was a fifteenth-century cannon founder, usually described as Hungarian, who offered his services to Sultan Mehmed II. He cast the giant bombards used by the Ottomans in the siege of Constantinople in 1453.

order-of-assassins.s: The Order of Assassins is the popular name for the Nizari Ismailis of Iran and Syria in the medieval period, founded under Hasan-i Sabbah in the Alborz mountains. Arising from the Fatimid succession crisis of 1094, they were known for targeted killings of political opponents.

organisation-of-african-unity.s: The Organisation of African Unity was an intergovernmental body of independent African states founded in Addis Ababa in 1963. Emperor Haile Selassie played a leading role in its creation.

orhan.s: Orhan was the second ruler of the Ottoman state, succeeding his father Osman I. He captured Bursa in 1326 and made it the dynasty's first proper capital.

orhogbua.s: Orhogbua was an Oba of Benin who reigned c. 1550–1578, during the height of the Benin Empire's power.

orkhon-inscriptions.s: The Orkhon inscriptions are monumental stone texts erected in the Orkhon valley of Mongolia between 732 and 735 CE by the Second Turkic Khaganate. Written in the Old Turkic runic script, they commemorate rulers and statesmen and reflect on the fate of the Turkic people.

oromo.s: The Oromo are a Cushitic-speaking people of the Horn of Africa, today one of the largest ethnic groups in Ethiopia. From the mid-sixteenth century Oromo pastoralists expanded into territories depopulated by the Ethiopian–Adal War.

oromo-migrations.s: The Oromo migrations were a large-scale expansion of Oromo-speaking pastoralists across the Horn of Africa from about 1565. They moved into lands weakened by the long war between Ethiopia and Adal.

orontes-river.s: The Orontes is a river of the northern Levant, flowing north through Lebanon, Syria and southern Turkey to the Mediterranean. The city of Kadesh stood on its banks.

osaka-castle.s: Osaka Castle is a fortress in Osaka built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in the late sixteenth century. It was the stronghold of the Toyotomi family after Hideyoshi's death.

osei-kwadwo.s: Osei Kwadwo was the Asantehene, or ruler of the Ashanti Empire, from 1764 to 1777. He introduced administrative reforms that based appointments on merit rather than solely on hereditary right.

osei-tutu-i.s: Osei Tutu I was the founder of the Ashanti Empire, uniting the Akan chiefdoms of the forest zone of present-day Ghana around the turn of the eighteenth century. Leading the Oyoko clan's state of Kumasi, he worked with the priest Okomfo Anokye, whose Golden Stool became the…

oskar-kokoschka.s: Oskar Kokoschka was an Austrian expressionist painter, printmaker and writer, born in 1886. He was part of the cultural flowering of Vienna at the turn of the twentieth century.

osman-i.s: Osman I was the founder of the Ottoman dynasty, a Turkoman chieftain of the Kayı clan of the Oghuz Turks, active around 1300. His beylik in Bithynia lay on the frontier with Byzantium and attracted ghazi warriors.

ostrich-feather.s: Ostrich feathers were a luxury trade good valued for decoration and fashion, carried north from the Sahel and Sahara across trans-Saharan routes. The Garamantian Empire traded them to Mediterranean markets in antiquity.

otto-i.s: Otto I, Duke of Saxony and King of Germany, was crowned emperor by Pope John XII in 962 CE. He had earlier defeated the Magyars at the Battle of Lechfeld in 955.

otto-von-bismarck.s: Otto von Bismarck was a Prussian statesman who unified Germany and served as the first chancellor of the German Empire. He built a federal constitution that preserved Prussian dominance among the empire's constituent states.

ottoman-conquest-of-egypt.s: The Ottoman conquest of Egypt was the campaign of Sultan Selim I that ended Mamluk rule in 1517. Following victory at Marj Dabiq in Syria in 1516, Ottoman forces took Cairo.

ottoman-empire.s: The Ottoman Empire was a Turkish Muslim state founded by Osman I around 1300 in north-western Anatolia, which grew to rule south-eastern Europe, the Middle East and North Africa. It conquered Constantinople in 1453, ending the Byzantine Empire, and absorbed the Mamluk…

ottoman-public-debt-administration.s: The Ottoman Public Debt Administration was an organisation established in 1881 after the Ottoman state defaulted on its foreign loans. Run by representatives of European creditors, it collected certain state revenues directly to service the debt.

ottoman-habsburg-wars.s: The Ottoman–Habsburg wars were a long series of conflicts between the Ottoman Empire and the Habsburg monarchy, fought from the sixteenth to the eighteenth century in Hungary, the Balkans and the Mediterranean. They included the sieges of Vienna in 1529 and 1683.

ottoman-mamluk-war-1516-1517.s: The Ottoman–Mamluk War was a conflict between the Ottoman Empire and the Mamluk Sultanate in 1516–1517. Ottoman victories at Marj Dabiq in Syria and Ridaniya near Cairo brought Syria, Egypt and the Hejaz under Ottoman rule in 1517.

ottoman-safavid-wars.s: The Ottoman–Safavid wars were a series of conflicts between the Sunni Ottoman Empire and the Shi'a Safavid Empire from the sixteenth to the eighteenth century. They were fought over eastern Anatolia, the Caucasus and Mesopotamia.

otuken.s: Ötüken is a sacred forested mountain region in central Mongolia, near the Orkhon valley, regarded by early Turkic peoples as the seat of legitimate rule. It was the political heartland of the Turkic khaganates.

ouidah.s: Ouidah is a coastal town in present-day Benin, one of the main ports of the Atlantic slave trade on the Bight of Benin. Captives taken in Oyo cavalry raids were sold to European merchants there in exchange for firearms, textiles and luxury goods.

overgrazing.s: Overgrazing occurs when livestock graze pasture more heavily than it can recover, degrading the land. On the steppe it reduced the resources available to pastoral societies.

ovimbundu.s: The Ovimbundu are a Bantu-speaking people of the central highlands of present-day Angola, active as long-distance traders in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. They took part in the trade in ivory and enslaved people reaching into the interior.

ovonramwen.s: Ovonramwen was the last independent Oba of the Benin Empire, who died in 1914. In 1897, after the killing of a British delegation, a British punitive expedition burned Benin City and looted its royal art.

owina-nido.s: The owina n'ido were the hereditary guild of weavers in the Benin Empire. Like the bronze-casters and ivory-carvers, they belonged to a system of royal craft guilds holding monopolies on particular luxury goods.

oxford.s: Oxford is a city in England, home to one of the oldest universities in Europe. In the medieval period it was among the universities where Roman law was studied.

oxus.s: The Oxus, now called the Amu Darya, is a major river of Central Asia flowing from the Pamirs towards the Aral Sea. It has long marked the boundary between Iran and the lands of Transoxiana.

oyo-empire.s: The Oyo Empire was a Yoruba state in the savannah of present-day western Nigeria, founded according to tradition by Oranmiyan. Its cavalry-based military enabled it to dominate a tributary network extending to Dahomey and the coast, especially in the seventeenth and eighteenth…

oyo-mesi.s: The Oyo Mesi was the council of seven hereditary chiefs, headed by the Basorun, that constrained the power of the Alaafin, the king of Oyo. Its collective authority could compel an Alaafin to abdicate.

oyo-ile.s: Oyo-Ile, also called Old Oyo or Katunga, was the capital of the Oyo Empire, located on open savannah in present-day north-western Nigeria. Its setting enabled the horse-based military culture on which Oyo's expansion depended.

oyoko-clan.s: The Oyoko clan is an Akan matrilineal clan whose leaders ruled the small state of Kumasi in the late seventeenth century. Osei Tutu, leader of the Oyoko, used this base to unite the Asante states.

ozolua.s: Ozolua, known as Ozolua the Conqueror, was an Oba of Benin who reigned c. 1480–1504.
